rows: Creative analysis – every creative since Sep 1, scored and explained (data to Tue Nov 24)

How to read: one bold row per creative (same video cut + same copy), with one row under it for every ad set it ran in (use outline 1/2 to collapse). Scores are 0–10 vs other ads optimising for the same event (10 = best; retention scores vs videos of the same length). Needs ₹1,000 spend to be scored. Hook = % of plays that watch past 15 s (ThruPlay). Skipped = plays that stopped before 15 s. Midroll = % of people at 25% of the video who reach 75%. Cliffhanger = % of people at 75% who reach the end. CTA = clicks per 100 ThruPlays (60%) + clicks that become installs / purchases (40%). Headline / description = copy rubric (curiosity question, conflict word, dialogue/emoji, length, app mention, named character). Overall = 40% CPI or cost per purchase + 15% hook + 15% CTA + 10% midroll + 10% cliffhanger + 5% headline + 5% description.

Meta does not report how long each person watched before clicking. "Est. watch before click" is a proxy: the point on the video's retention curve where the number of people still watching equals the number of clickers (assumes clickers are the most engaged viewers); when it equals the length, fewer people clicked than finished, i.e. clickers typically watch to the end – then "Clicks per 100 who watched to the end" shows how well the ending converts. Avg watch can exceed the length because Meta counts replays/loops. Observations update daily; the history cell only gets a new dated line when the picture changes.
